analyst.summary: APL Apollo remains India's dominant structural steel tube maker (55-60% share) with a fortress balance sheet (D/E 0.09x, ROCE 31.1%) and a credible, self-funded capacity roadmap (5 MT to 8 MT by FY28), but Q1 FY27 volumes fell 6% YoY -- a fresh, verified miss against the company's own 15-20% FY27 growth guidance -- driven by HRC-price-spike-triggered channel destocking and soft Dubai utilization. Brokerages (Nuvama, Motilal Oswal, JM Financial) all trimmed FY27 estimates but retained Buy/Add ratings, reading this as transient rather than a demand break. At ~41-42x trailing earnings against a historical 12.6% 3-year revenue CAGR, the market is pricing sustained high-teens-to-20%+ earnings growth that the realized volume trend is not currently delivering, and the PIT data confirms the underlying margin-volatility risk is real (Sep-2024 quarter net profit collapsed to Rs 54 crore on a steel-price-driven inventory loss). No balance-sheet or governance red flags. Call: Hold the existing position, not Sell -- the moat and balance sheet are intact -- but this is not a name to add to at current multiples, and it should be watched closely into H2 FY27 for whether the volume-growth guidance gap closes or widens.
